prompt: Render any list of rows as an aligned text table where each column is described by a Function that extracts its cell text; pad every column but the last to its widest entry.
explanation: Describing a column as a Function<T, String> means the table code never needs to know what a row is -- the caller supplies the extraction, so the same renderer formats StockLines and plain Strings. Because widths depend on every cell, the method has to collect all the text before it can emit a single line, which is why the cells are built into a list of lists first. Skipping the padding on the final column is what keeps lines free of trailing whitespace, and returning early on an empty row list avoids printing a header for a table with no data.
hints: Build a List<List<String>> where element 0 is the headers and the rest are the extracted cells, then every width is widestOf on one column of that structure.
For column c, pad only while c is not the last index: `while (cell.length() < widths[c]) cell = cell + " ";`.
Join cells with " | " and lines with "\n" by appending the separator BEFORE each element except the first, so nothing trails at the end.
